ops.entry: WHEN output is operator-facing prose or a printed command DO consume it as the operator would — read prose for truth; shell-split each printed command with a spaced fixture root, run it verbatim, and assert it reaches the intended target. Substring and sweep gates prove presence, never truth or runnability.
ops.why: Relayed QA1 accepted: my green c1 suite asserted printed-command substrings while every command was unrunnable (glued punctuation, unquoted root, bare script); only verbatim copy-running caught it. Merged with G-05's prose-truth rule, same root: token gates cannot prove what the text does.

ops.entry: WHEN a rule has several legs or orders its checks DO give each leg its own discriminating row, and each ordering a row where both checks fire asserting which cause wins — a memoized, lazily re-invoked check, or inputs tripping one check, leave narrowing and reorder mutants green.
ops.why: Two ordering mutants survived across cycles (placement after preflight hidden by a lazily re-invoked memoized check; feature check after persona check) plus a dropped isinstance leg; P-06 covered legs but not order.

ops.entry: WHEN fail-first needs a pre-fix red and source edits are refused DO load the old blob into a fresh in-process module, or run the new tests in a whole old-SHA tree — subprocess cases and fixtures copying the subject re-read disk, so partial swaps run new code.
ops.why: My whole-tree base reproduction found 110 reds against the author's 89: fixtures copying bin/ still ran the live guard. Sharpens P-07's why to cover fixture copies, not only subprocess re-imports.

originals.original: WHEN every gate on a diff is token- or phrase-based (grep/sweep) DO recognize none of them can confirm replacement prose is actually true — only that a token is present or absent. A false statement that satisfies every sweep is caught only by reading the prose directly.

WHEN a rule excludes or includes entries via multiple distinct triggering legs (e.g. two ways an item can match) DO verify each leg has its own test case — a suite pinning only one leg lets a regression narrowing an untested leg ship silently while the pinned leg keeps passing.

WHEN fail-first needs a pre-fix red and source edits are refused DO load the old blob (`git show <sha>:<path>`) into a fresh in-process module, or check the new tests into an old-SHA pin — cases spawning subprocesses re-import from disk, so only the pin reddens them.

ops.entry: WHEN writing, copying or deleting under bash-write-guard DO use literal absolute targets — variable-bearing redirect, cp or rm targets are blocked even under /tmp or notes/; clean up inside a python driver. `git checkout` is refused even in a /tmp clone: use `git archive <sha> | tar -x`.
ops.why: Observed this feature: git checkout refused inside a /tmp clone; git archive gave a source-identical tree without moving HEAD. Same guard as G-13, so merged rather than displacing another entry.

originals.original: WHEN writing, copying or deleting under bash-write-guard DO use literal absolute target paths — a redirect, cp or rm target containing a shell variable is blocked even under /tmp or the feature's notes/; do temp cleanup inside a python driver and pipe rather than redirect in loops.
